input.summary:
Parents' bedroom furnished in parts/room-9.mjs: red bed head to the west wall (x 10, z 9), barrel nightstands with lit candles and a lantern, a chest barrel, flower-pot window boxes under the north windows, a bookshelf wardrobe in the east corner, a white rug, and hanging lanterns at (14,22,9) and (17,22,10).
make.sh gives a whole build.nbt; this part places 26 blocks with no REFUSED or off-palette writes. `mcd room` says OK, walk ok, min light 9, no dim or dark cells.
The one room check at the end flagged 1 cell (10,21,11) as unreached, which I did not resolve; the verdict is still OK.

waste.what: Floor grid from `mcd plan` was stale: it showed x 9 as free floor, but the shell's bricks wall sits at x 9 for y 19..22, so my first layout was refused on 5 cells and I had to shift the whole furniture one column east.
waste.cost: one make.sh rebuild plus one re-layout (about 2 minutes)
waste.tool: `mcd plan` should read the built build.nbt's actual blocks (shell and earlier parts) when it prints the floor, not the plan's rectangle; or `runParts` should print the refused cells before the part is written

waste.what: Probed individual cells one at a time with a throwaway node script to find out which blocks were in the room.
waste.tool: `mcd cell build.nbt x,y,z ...` or the plan's floor grid showing block names for occupied cells, not only 'o'

waste.what: Chose bed, barrel, candle and lantern states by reading `mcd states` one block at a time, then wrote the legend by hand.
waste.tool: a legend helper that accepts a block name and fills in valid default states (facing/part for beds, hanging for lanterns)

companions.task: build the wardrobe as real doors on an oak cabinet, and make the bed frame and nightstands from spruce stairs and slabs instead of barrels, so the furniture reads as built rather than stored

left: Walk verdict lists one unreached floor cell (10,21,11) out of 43; the room check still says OK, so I did not confirm whether it is a real gap or a counting quirk.

The wardrobe is a bookshelf stack, not a door-fronted cabinet; the nightstands and chest are barrels, not stairs, slabs or trapdoors. Good enough for a glance, but a joiner could make them read as furniture.
plan.md's bedroom floor grid is stale: the shell puts a bricks wall at x 9 (y 19..22) that the plan treats as free floor, so the usable room is x 10..18. The plan or shell needs reconciling.
plan.md's checklist has no room item to tick and elements.md has no bedroom element, so nothing was ticked; the lighting item (element 24) is only partly covered by my two hanging lanterns.
